exposure: preterm first birth (extremely preterm, very preterm, late preterm)
cohort: The study included 213,335 women in Norway who gave birth to their first and second singleton child between 1999 and 2014.
finding: A previous preterm first birth was a major risk factor for a preterm second birth, with the contribution of placental disorders being more pronounced for recurrent extremely and very preterm birth than for recurrent late preterm birth.
gest_age: Outcomes were categorized by gestational age: <28+0 weeks (extremely preterm), 28+0-33+6 weeks (very preterm), and 34+0-36+6 weeks (late preterm), with overall preterm birth defined as <37 weeks.
